queue.title: sy98 model vs the real stale sMarioScreenY ($A23B) register
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (the up-lock latch test) + the 18-capture gate, measured byte-identical with the fix
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-14, by measurement rather than by changing the model first (which is what this item asked for).
WHAT WAS WRONG: the `$0D97` tail of `$0C7D` is `ldh a,[$FFC0] / ld [sPrevMarioY],a` - it latches the LIVE Mario Y. The up-lock warp (`home.asm:1782-1790`) writes `$FFC0 = 0` and then falls into that same tail, so on the warp frame the ROM latches 0 while the port latched the value the body entered with, leaving the next frame's `dv = $FFC0 - sPrevMarioY` short by the pre-warp low byte on every frame after an up transition. Fixed: `CameraSim::step` now ends with `self.prev_mario_y_lo = sim.y as u8` (the live byte) instead of the entry snapshot `my_lo`.
MEASURED FIRST (the item's own recommendation): a temporary probe tracked both latches frame by frame. Body-warps DO fire - 8 of the 18 captures (traj10, traj11, traj12, traj13, traj14, traj16, death3, screen_transition1), one each - and the `dv` branch classification (zero / < $80 / >= $80) differs on 0 frames in all 18. The decisive A/B is the gate itself, because the camera moves by dv's MAGNITUDE and not just its branch: with the live latch the 18-capture gate is byte-identical to the pre-fix run. So the fix is fidelity, not a level-1 behaviour change - which also matches the note's own reading that the register's readers are the two lock rows the transition ends never straddle with a stale value.
TEST: one new camera test (`the_up_lock_warp_latches_the_warped_y_not_the_entry_value`) drives the real warp arm (camera on the `$48` lock row with edge bit2, Mario's Y lo $C0 against a latch of 0 for the `>= $80` up branch and `sy98 = $1A < $1B`) and asserts the warp, `sim.y = 0`, and the latch reading 0 rather than $C0. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix model ($C0) and pass with it, so it pins the behaviour rather than describing it.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE - the other half of the conflation: `prev_mario_y_lo` is still one field for two ROM bytes. The movement role now correctly models `sPrevMarioY` ($A20C); the `$C0`/`$48` hard-edge reads want the draw's `sMarioScreenY` ($A23B), modelled as `sy98 = prev_mario_y_lo - cam_y_lo + $62`. Splitting it into two fields would be unverifiable by any capture (the two bytes differ only on frames where the register is not consulted: the first frame after `$0F2A`, transition frames, parked frames) and the note's recommendation was to keep the sy98 model, which this item's measurements now support. If a future capture shows a lock-row divergence at a transition end, that is the first thing to split.

queue.title: $532D spin-jump pose: its $FF97 & $0C table index needs bit 3, which captures do not record
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (the pose test) - the capture half of the gate is NOT satisfiable today; see note
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-14, ported and unit-tested. The capture half of the gate is NOT satisfiable as written; this note says exactly why and what it would take.
THE ROM, quoted (main.asm:210-243): `$530D` stores $FFBB = 1, then reads `sPipeTravelDirection`; below $10 it falls into `$532D`, which is `ld a,[sSpinJump] / and a / jr z,$534C` else `ld hl,$5348 / ldh a,[$FF97] / and $0C / srl a / srl a / ld e,a / ld d,0 / add hl,de / ld a,[hl] / ldh [$FFC6],a / jp $5447`. The table at `$5348` is `db $04, $10, $00, $11`, indexed by `($FF97 & $0C) >> 2`. So the spin pose is four frames cycling on $FF97 bits 3-2, it OVERRIDES every other pose, and `$5447` then applies the powerup offset on top (+32 small / +69 bunny / +112 fire) - so a spinning small Mario shows $24, a spinning fire Mario $74.
ORDERING, the part the port had to get right: `$530D` tests the pipe direction FIRST and `$532D` is only reached below $10, so a spinning Mario in a pipe still shows the pipe frame ($10/$20 -> 16, $30 -> walk+1, $40 -> walk+5). In the port that is a branch inserted between `frame_index`'s pipe-dir arm and the grounded/ducking chain.
WHAT LANDED (crates/sml2-core/src/player_sim.rs): `PlayerSim::SPIN_JUMP_FRAMES = [0x04, 0x10, 0x00, 0x11]` and the `$532D` branch in `frame_index`; test `the_spin_jump_pose_overrides_every_other_frame` covering all four frames ($FF97 = $00/$04/$08/$0C), the wrap case $14, the override of the AIR pose as well as the standing one, the pipe-direction precedence, and the normal pose returning once the spin clears. Big Mario (`powerup = 1`) in the test so the $5447 offset is 0 and the table values are visible as-is.
THE INDEX IS BUILT FROM TWO SOURCES, deliberately: bit 2 from `phase` (the capture-validated low bits of $FF97) and bit 3 from `frame_counter`. The captures can only check the low bits, so a replay keeps bit 2 exactly right and only bit 3 is best-effort. The replay loop also increments `frame_counter` now instead of leaving it at 0.
WHY THE CAPTURE GATE CANNOT COVER IT: the capture record carries three bits of $FF97 (the `phase` field, which the replay seeds from). Bit 3 is not in the format at all. Two further facts make this harder than it looks: (a) `$FF97` is FREE-RUNNING from boot - its only writers are `inc a / ldh [$FF97],a` at home.asm:349-351 and home.asm:5170-5172, both gated on $FF82 and both plain increments, with no reset anywhere, so bit 3 carries an arbitrary boot-time offset that persists into the level; (b) the spin jump needs `hKeysHeld` bit 7 (down) + `sCurPowerup` bit 0 (big or fire) + `sMarioOnGround == 0` + `sMoonPhysics & $0F == 0` (home.asm:2529-2556, which is also what writes `sSpinJump`), and level 1's captures never collect a mushroom - the measured item ids there are 6 and 7 only. So the remaining capture work is: add a $FF97 bit-3 field to the capture format, then record a spin jump in a level that hands out a mushroom. That is a capture-format change plus harness work, not a one-off probe, which is why it is left as this item's honest remainder rather than quietly skipped.
FIDELITY NOTE: because of (a), even with bit 3 recorded a replay would have to be TOLD the counter value rather than deriving it - the console's bit 3 at level entry is an artifact of the number of frames the machine had run since boot.

queue.title: Golden coins (sGoldenCoin1-6 $A84D-$A865) and the map-side tally ($307BC / $30884)
queue.verification_gate: cargo test (4 tests: the fold, the charge/wipe/wrap, the no-coin path, the save offsets)
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-14. The MECHANISM is now modelled end to end; the AWARD is decided out of scope, deliberately, and this note records both.
THE ROM, quoted. CASTLE SCREEN (main.asm:17058 `$307BC`): `xor a / ld [sGoldenCoinCount],a`, then for each coin `ld a,[sGoldenCoinN] / bit 7,a / jr z,...` -> stage the sprite ids `[$498A]`/`[$49A2]`/`[$49BA]` (1637 lines apart per coin) through `$2B13` and `inc`s `sGoldenCoinCount`. The six are tested in the order 1, 2, 6, 5, 4, 3. LOSS PATH (home.asm:5280-5320, inside `$27AF`): after `sLives = 5`, `sCoinLow/High = 0`, `sMoneyBagCount = 0`, `ld b,0` then for the same six, in the same order, `and $80 / sla a / rl b` - folding each coin's bit 7 into successive bits of `sGoldenCoinFlags` (bit 5 = coin 1 ... bit 0 = coin 3) - then `ld [sGoldenCoinFlags],a`; `ld b,6 / ld c,0` and a six-iteration `srl a / jr nc,+ / inc c` popcount; `ld a,[sLevelTally] / sub c / daa / ld [sLevelTally],a`; `xor a` into all six coin bytes; `call $2934` (the save); then `sFadeTimerLow = 255`, `sMusicRequest = 7`, `$FF9B = 7`. So a game over CHARGES the tally one point per golden coin AND WIPES all six. `$30884` (state `$07`'s per-frame draw) tests `sGoldenCoinFlags` bit 5 - coin 1 - which is why the fold has to precede the wipe.
ADDRESSES: sGoldenCoin1 $A84D, coin2 $A851, coin3 $A856, coin4 $A859, coin5 $A85F, coin6 $A865 (ram.asm:685-701); sGoldenCoinFlags $A2B5; sGoldenCoinCount $A2CB. Relative to the persisted `sLevelProgress` block at `$A848`, that is +5/+9/+14/+17/+23/+29 - i.e. save-record offsets +$0D/+$11/+$16/+$19/+$1F/+$25, which the `$2934` record carries verbatim because `save_record` copies the whole block.
WHAT LANDED (crates/sml2-core/src/player_sim.rs): `bcd_sub` (the `sub c / daa` with the borrow that wraps: 12-3 = 09, 05-6 = $99, matching `daa` rather than going negative); `PlayerSim::GOLDEN_COINS = [5, 9, 29, 23, 17, 14]` - the offsets IN `$27AF`'s FOLD ORDER, so element 0 is the flags byte's bit 5; `golden_coin_flags()` (the fold, from the persisted bytes); `golden_coin_count()` (following `$307BC`: derived from the six BYTES, which is why it reads 0 once `$27AF` has wiped them - the two derivations agree before the clear, which is exactly when `$27AF` uses its own); a `golden_coin_flags` field for `sGoldenCoinFlags`; and `game_over_enter`, which now folds, charges the BCD tally, wipes the six bytes and leaves the flags - the `$2934` save it then makes is built on demand by `save_record` (no SRAM).
THE DECISION, stated plainly: the award is OUT OF SCOPE, because the ROM has no writer for any of the six bytes' bit 7 anywhere (an exhaustive baserom scan of `ld [$A84x],a` / `ld hl,$A84x` / `ld a,[$A84x]` / pointer pairs / `set 7,(hl)` finds none). A bit-faithful port therefore reproduces a game in which a golden coin can never be collected, and this port does not invent one. What it DOES do is model every consumer, so that a save loaded with those bits set behaves exactly as the ROM would: the castle screen's icon row and `sGoldenCoinCount`, the state-$07 icon, the fold, the tally charge and the wipe. IF AN AWARD IS EVER SUPPLIED it must set bit 7 - every consumer tests only that bit - and everything downstream then follows automatically.
VERIFIED: 128 tests. New: `golden_coin_flags_fold_in_the_roms_order` (each of the six slots individually - which is what would catch a transposed fold - all six, and a byte with the other seven bits set contributing nothing), `game_over_charges_the_tally_and_wipes_the_golden_coins` (12h - 2 = 10h, the flags kept at $30 while the bytes wipe, the 05h - 6 = $99 wrap, and the no-coin case leaving the tally alone), and `the_golden_coin_bytes_are_the_save_records_offsets` (each byte showing up at its documented record offset, which pins `GOLDEN_COINS` to the save layout as well as to `$27AF`). The 18-capture gate is clean and note-free, its only visible divergence traj4_ff0's documented legacy one; the death captures reach `game_over_enter`, but only ever down the no-coin path, which is the case the third test pins.

SYMPTOM: x=637 mismatches of 1308 compared frames; the first is f36 ('frame 36: x sim=64 exp=63') and the pattern is a persistent +1 with the sim AHEAD, recurring on ~637 frames - i.e. on the frames the autoscroll camera steps (654 of 1308) - while every other check is all-zero: camx, camy, edge, en_r, en_l, y, hvel, vvel, ground, timer, dir, frame, uphase, ff0. RULED OUT by reading, so do not re-investigate: (a) the clamp's ARITHMETIC - player_sim.rs:1438-1444 is a byte-exact transliteration of $0FBF/$0FD1/$0FE3 (b = x - camx + 96; b < $10 -> x += 16-b; b >= $A0 -> x -= b-160; both with the carry/borrow into the high byte) and the no-clamp window (b in [$10,$A0), i.e. screen X in [0..63] u [176..255]) matches the ROM exactly; (b) the FRAME ORDER - the ROM calls the player update BEFORE the camera (home.asm:799 `call $0F71`, then home.asm:803 `call $0B2A`), exactly what both port loops do (main.rs:1270 sim.step, then 1296 cam.step), so the clamp reads the PREVIOUS frame's camera byte in both; (c) the PAIRING - a one-frame shift error would move camx too, and camx matches on all 1308 frames. WHAT IS LEFT: the console moves Mario differently from the port ONLY on the frames the camera advances, and the camera's own output is identical either way ($0DAF ignores Mario). Candidates, cheapest first: (1) WHERE inside $0F71 the clamp runs relative to the X integration and the $1413 push-out - home.asm:2119's call site (what gates it, and what runs between it and $181C's integration) against the port's order (push-out at 1256, integration at 1425-1426, clamp at 1438); (2) whether the console's $0DAF frame reaches Mario through a path the port's autoscroll branch skips (the port dispatches `if auto_scroll != 0 { run_autoscroll } else { $0B5E/$0BE5 }`); (3) a within-frame write order on the camera byte the clamp reads. METHOD, do not guess: offline per-frame delta analysis over the capture's own records - for each mismatching frame pair the recorded (x, camx) with the port's model and find the rule that reproduces the console's x; then price the candidate fix over the whole capture AND the 19-capture sweep. THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE CLAMP - it was the VALUE FED TO IT: `run_replay` did `sim.camx = f.camx as u16; sim.camy = f.camy as u16;` (the record's camera) while `run_play` already latched the port's own `cam.x`/`cam.y`. TWO CANDIDATE MODELS BOTH FIT and no measurement on this corpus separates them - (landed) latch the sim's own camera object vs (alternative) inject the PREVIOUS record's camx/camy; they are byte-equivalent on all 1309 records because the camx/camy checks stay all-zero either way. The derivation was landed because it removes the injection class rather than re-timing it. retired_capture_tasks.note: PLANNED 2026-10-14 (plan phase P1), not started. WHY IT EXISTS: traj17 is the first capture to reach a level clear, and it ends ON the $14 hand-off frame - so `map_handoff_14_body` is marked done while its own note admits the body is unexercised. Nothing has ever run $3EF2B / $3F003 against the console. HOW: traj17 already proves the two-hook splice works ($05E4 for state $04, $028D for every other state), so extend the same route past the arm with the $028D hook and let the post-hand-off frames record; the state machine from $14 into $0C is input-dependent and unmodelled, so use the GAP technique (poll $FF9B per tick, attach `gap: {total, seq}` to the first post-gap record) exactly as death_capture2 does for the death cycle. This is also the first console look at state $0C, which is what `overworld_map_state_0C` needs. Two hooks, one pairing: both sample the same frame boundary, so apply_pairing.py is unchanged. SPEC COMPLETE 2026-10-14 (notes/traj18_tail_spec.md, deleg_01406b1d task 4; read-only, from the ROM plus probe runs - every inference is listed in the spec's inference_only section). STATE SEQUENCE, quoted: the arm frame sets $FF9B=24 ($18) with sFadeTimer=192; 192 deterministic frames of state $18 (the VBlank decrements the fade once per frame, no pad read); the fade's LAST frame charges sLevelTally 00->01 and writes $FF9B=20 ($14) - that frame DOES produce a $028D record (it is traj17's last record); the $14 body ($3EF2B) then runs as ONE dispatch spanning 21-22 wall-clock frames with ZERO $028D fires, doing the palette swap $E4/$D0/$39, sLevelProgress[$650E[node]] set-7/res-3, the $3F024 node move to $14 + progress bit 7, then $2934's save and $FF9B=12; the first $0C frame reaches $028D 11-13 ticks later (gap total 33-35). CHECKS (raw address + expected on a plain level-1 bell clear): $A840=$14, $A848=$80, $A2C5=$01, $A27D=$00 (NOT written by the hand-off), $A2B4=$00, and the save image at $A000+0: node=$14, progress=$80, +$40..$44 = 00 00 01 05 00, +$45 the checksum, +$46..$49 the 12 34 56 78 signature. HARNESS CHANGE (small, the spec quotes the lines to mirror): add optional node/prog/lvl9b/save fields to Frame; push node/prog in the per-frame block beside the exit/tally pushes; dispatch the gap handler on g.seq.first() and for $14 validate acct == g.total - NOT the death relation 1+sum(seq)==total, which is measured here as sum(seq)==total (34==34, 35==35) - printing a 'level-clear hand-off:' line; then a post-loop one-shot that validates the captured save image with map::save_record_valid against sim.save_record(obj.money_bag) field by field. No pairing change is needed; the existing exit_arm block needs none either, but its comment and the README's traj17 wording should say the tally frame DOES fire $028D and the frame that never reaches it is the $14 body's. CUT POINT: right after the FIRST post-hand-off record ($FF9B == $0C), because the hub then rewrites sMapNode and walks sMapCursorMove. The 33-35-tick gap is probe-measured and must be re-measured on the real route, never assumed.
